title: The Clock Beneath the Well
paras: On a volcanic plateau, a borehole drilled for irrigation unexpectedly became a geyser. Its eruptions resembled the strokes of a [[piston|piston]], although no machinery remained underground. A narrow passage connected the surface to a chamber of heated groundwater, converting continuous heating into intermittent motion.

At depth, pressure [[invariably|invariably]] raises water's boiling point above its surface value. The chamber's contents can therefore exceed 100°C without boiling. Eventually, escaping bubbles lift water out of the passage, reducing pressure below. Some remaining water abruptly becomes steam, driving an eruption that largely empties the chamber.

An archive records how a [[peasant|peasant]] farming beside the borehole feared an irrigation contractor would [[monopolize|monopolize]] the water. Following the site manager's [[resignation|resignation]], her replacement offered a [[tactful|tactful]] compromise: shared access between eruptions. However, scalding overflows forced operators to [[amend|amend]] their distribution plan, while a safety inspection made fencing [[mandatory|mandatory]]. The underground cycle, not the timetable, determined when collection was possible.

Today, a monitoring circuit drawing less than one [[ampere|ampere]] records temperature changes before each discharge. Yet regularity does not imply permanence. Mineral deposits gradually constrict the passage, while fractures can divert its supply. Unlike a [[mortal|mortal]] organism, the geyser does not undergo biological ageing, but it can cease functioning. Its final silence may result not from cooling rocks but from changes in its hidden plumbing.
zh: 在一片火山高原上，一口为灌溉而钻的井意外变成了间歇泉。它的喷发如同活塞的往复运动，尽管地下已没有任何机械设备。一条狭窄通道将地表与一个储存受热地下水的腔室连接起来，把持续加热转化为间歇性的运动。
在地下深处，压力总会使水的沸点高于地表条件下的沸点。因此，腔室里的水即使超过100摄氏度，也可能仍未沸腾。最终，逸出的气泡将水推出通道，使下方压力降低。剩余的水有一部分随即迅速变成蒸汽，引发一次喷发，将腔室内的大部分水排出。
一份档案记载，一位在钻井旁耕作的小农担心某个灌溉承包商会垄断水源。现场女负责人辞职后，继任者委婉地提出一个折中方案：在两次喷发之间共同取水。然而，滚烫的水溢出，迫使运营人员修改配水计划，而一次安全检查又要求必须设置围栏。决定何时能够取水的，是地下的循环过程，而非时间表。
如今，一套电流不足一安培的监测电路记录着每次喷发前的温度变化。然而，规律性并不意味着永久不变。矿物沉积物逐渐使通道变窄，裂隙则可能使供水改道。与终有一死的生物不同，间歇泉不会经历生物性衰老，却仍然可能停止活动。它最终归于沉寂，可能不是因为岩石冷却，而是因为其隐蔽的地下管道发生了变化。

q.s: The borehole was originally intended to provide water for agriculture.
q.why: 首段说明钻井原本用于灌溉。

q.s: The eruption begins when pressure inside the underground chamber increases suddenly.
q.why: 第二段指出压力下降使部分水骤变为蒸汽。

q.s: The replacement manager had previously supervised another geothermal site.
q.why: 文章未提及继任负责人的工作经历。
